**No, the first wave may not start.** The preflight record is for a different night: its window is 2026-11-13 22:00Z to 2026-11-14 08:00Z, and tonight is 2026-11-21. Even for that night it would fail on an expiring token and a test account two packages share. Also, the plan is not marked unattended, so the plan check that passed was not the check an overnight run needs.

**Why it matters:** if the run starts on this record, the repository token is already dead (it expired 2026-11-14 03:00Z). P1 and P2 would also both act as the same order-clerk account at the same time. The run would stall or produce results you can't trust while nobody is watching, and the gate would refuse it at the end (`PREFLIGHT_REQUIRED`).

**Do this first:**
1. In `.alchemy/runs/r1/plan.json`, set `execution.unattended: true` and add `needs` to P1, P2 and P3. Each package with a command check also needs an `environment` need. Then run the plan check again and note the `plan_digest` it prints.
2. Rewrite `.alchemy/runs/r1/preflight.json` with that digest and base `3f9c2e1` in a `plan` field, and tonight's window. Also fix the token, the account and the `covers` lists described under Findings.
3. Run `python .claude/skills/alchemy-orchestrate/scripts/check_orchestration.py preflight .alchemy/runs/r1/preflight.json --plan .alchemy/runs/r1/plan.json --profile alchemy-workspace.json --root .` and start only on `PASS`.

- I didn't read `alchemy-workspace.json`, so I haven't checked whether the profile requires other needs (`preflight.needs`) or whether every verification command it lists has a passing baseline record. Running the checker in step 3 with `--profile` closes this.
- I found no record that the human approved the plan. Run the plan check with `--approved <digest>` once the lead approves.
- "22:00 tonight" doesn't say a time zone, and the record uses UTC. Confirm with the lead before writing the new window.
